evidence: Single Python package 'trackeval' with clear module boundaries (datasets, metrics, baselines, utils, plotting, eval)
High cohesion within modules (e.g., all dataset implementations inherit from _BaseDataset, all metrics inherit from _BaseMetric)
Low coupling between modules (modules import only specific components, no tight interdependencies)
Centralized entry points (scripts/run_*.py) that import and orchestrate trackeval components
No external service communication or network dependencies in core modules
Shared core abstractions (_BaseDataset, _BaseMetric) used consistently across domain areas
Directory structure reflects domain decomposition (datasets/, metrics/, baselines/) rather than technical layers
risks: Some scripts import trackeval directly without clear separation between CLI and core logic
Baseline modules contain multiprocessing logic mixed with domain logic, reducing modularity
Shared utilities (utils.py) may become a god module over time
